newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo NBY sells bonds from its portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Yugo NBY sells bonds from its portfolio.

text.p: Yugoslavia's central bank put part of its bond portfolio on sale to compensate for funds previously given to Serbia's Commodity Reserve Agency to finance grain stockpiling.

The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) offered for sale two tranches of 6-month bonds issued by the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency, totalling 88.8 million dinars ($16.04 million), head of trading at the Belgrade bourse Gordana Dostanic said.
The bond's face value is 10,000 dinars and carries an interest equivalent to the NBY's discount rate, set at a monthly 2.5 percent for April, Dostanic said.

"Targetted buyers are commercial banks who get a chance to activate half of the funds set aside in the form of their reserve requirement with the NBY. They will collect interest payment each month" she told Reuters. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
